name: Rattan Vipers
headerMeta: Silver era · Ranged infantry · special · 155 leadership · Honor Tree
pitch: Rattan Vipers are a poison-stacking support archer that wins by neutering enemy damage output rather than by killing directly. Keep it shooting instead of meleeing — especially against large shields — and feed it a rate-of-fire doctrine for the extra Poison Barrage volley, since ammo consumption is the main thing that shuts it down.

doctrines.name: Poisons Doctrine V
doctrines.note: +140 all AP, +60 poison DMG, stacks up to 2x — most of the unit's strength comes from the Poison Barrage passive, rarely worth stacking on one target

doctrines.name: Precision Doctrine V
doctrines.note: +120 piercing DMG, +80 piercing AP, +9% rate of fire

doctrines.name: Bowmanship Doctrine V
doctrines.note: Arrow Rain +75% base piercing per hit, +150 piercing DMG

veterancy.label: Top Line
veterancy.body: Maximizes Poison Barrage (spell 2) — 3 volleys by default, 4 with Vet ROF plus a rate-of-fire doctrine, all applying the Poison Spread passive; massively increases impact during blob pushes. {1} An older source disagrees, rejecting Top Line's rate-of-fire/armor-pen bonuses as pushing toward raw damage — "not this unit's job." {2}

veterancy.label: Bottom Line
veterancy.body: Constant DPS, hitting isolated units repeatedly to stack the poison passive on them — situational, mainly against small groups (rare) per the current guide. {1} The older source calls this the unambiguous pick instead, stacking movement speed, bonus-hit chance, poison-duration, and attack-slow to reinforce the debuff role. {2}

battleRole.positioning: Use ordinary circle targeting (ability slot 1) to keep the unit shooting instead of dropping bows for melee when enemies close — explicitly recommended against large-shield units so the archers don't waste bow-guard uptime. {2}
battleRole.tips: Ammo consumption is the unit's known weak point; a Sprint-type doctrine has been suggested as a way to manage it. {2}

cards.name: Namkhan Archers
cards.why: a house member claims Vipers outperform them at wall pushes in Territory Wars for the same slot — a self-labeled personal opinion, flagged likely-stale and unverified against current patch

matchups.pressure: You pressure: large shield/spear lines and cavalry (attrition without landing meaningful damage once stacked, cavalry survivable only behind cover), Iron Reapers and Claymores (lose most damage output mid-charge once poison stacks apply), Shenji Grenadiers and Glaive-wielding heroes ("completely useless" against a properly stacked engagement) — per a 2022 source flagged for a current-patch sanity check. {2}

controls.notes: Poison Barrage (spell 2) fires 3 volleys by default; Vet ROF plus a rate-of-fire doctrine (e.g. Precision V's +9%) adds a 4th, each volley applying the Poison Spread passive. {1} Poison stacks up to 5 times, cutting a fully-stacked target's damage output by roughly 71% on average per the source's own testing. {2} No input-loop press-sequence is documented for this unit — only the circle-targeting mode setting covered under battle role.

gaps: No Strength-by-fight-type ratings exist for this unit in the Amya guide or unit-db (fightRatings null) — recorded as a gap, not fabricated.
Amya's OP gives no Counters section and no Hero-pairing for this unit — both explicit source gaps.

A 2022 video source gives a different doctrine build (Accuracy/Arrow Rain mandatory, Breakthrough/Epic Archery filling remaining slots, a Sprint-type suggestion) than the current Amya/unit-db list and flags itself as pre-patch — left out of the doctrines list rather than merged, since the two builds aren't cleanly reconcilable.
